section: Forest and wildlife legal framework - Indian Forest Act 1927, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972
subsections: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology
WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin
Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment

accepted.s:
Arrange the following laws and policies in chronological order of their enactment or adoption:
A. National Forest Policy, 1952
B. Indian Forest Act, 1927
C. Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
D. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
o: B, A, C, D
A, B, C, D
B, C, A, D
A, C, B, D
accepted.x: The correct sequence is the Indian Forest Act, 1927, National Forest Policy, 1952, Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last dates to eliminate sequences before checking the middle entries.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first Indian Forest Act was drafted in which year?
accepted.x: The first Indian Forest Act was drafted in 1865.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first forest legislation from the later consolidating Act of 1927.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following features is associated with the Indian Forest Act, 1878?
o: It established the Animal Welfare Board of India.
It created the Concurrent List for forests and wildlife.
It introduced the 33% forest and tree cover target.
It introduced reserved, protected and village forests.
accepted.x: The Indian Forest Act, 1878 introduced the categories of reserved, protected and village forests.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive institutional feature with the correct law and year.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Indian Forest Act, 1927 is best described as a law that
o: consolidated colonial forest legislation and continues to remain in force
created the National Forest Policy after Independence
regulated only wildlife sanctuaries and national parks
transferred forests exclusively to the State List
accepted.x: The Indian Forest Act, 1927 was a colonial consolidating law and continues to remain in force.
accepted.tq: Select the precise description rather than an option that confuses a forest law with a policy or constitutional provision.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act was enacted in 1960.
2. The Animal Welfare Board of India was set up under this Act in 1962.
3. The Act transferred forests and wildlife to the Concurrent List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Transfer of forests and wildlife to the Concurrent List was associated with the 42nd Amendment in 1976, not the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that assigns a constitutional change to the wrong legislation.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment is significant for forest and wildlife governance because it
o: inserted Articles 48A and 51A(g) and placed forests and wildlife in the Concurrent List
created Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act
established the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
introduced the village forest category
accepted.x: The 42nd Amendment inserted Article 48A, added Article 51A(g), and transferred forests and wildlife to the Concurrent List.
accepted.tq: Associate a constitutional amendment with its specific Articles and legislative-list change.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Forest Policy, 1988?
o: It brought forests into the Concurrent List.
It set a target of 33% forest and tree cover.
It abolished the Indian Forest Act, 1927.
It created the first three forest categories under Indian law.
accepted.x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 set the target of 33% forest and tree cover.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy-specific target instead of confusing it with statutory or constitutional changes.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 came into force on
o: 5 June 1986
25 October 1980
26 January 1981
15 August 1980
accepted.x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 came into force on 25 October 1980.
accepted.tq: Test the exact commencement date rather than merely the enactment year.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Environment (Protection) Act — 1986
2. Biological Diversity Act — 2002
3. Forest Rights Act — 2006
4. Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act — 2022
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched: the Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in 1986, the Biological Diversity Act in 2002, the Forest Rights Act in 2006, and the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act in 2022.
accepted.tq: Check each year-law pair independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 renamed the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 as the
o: National Forest Protection Adhiniyam, 1980
Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980
Van Jeevan Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2023
Bharatiya Van Adhiniyam, 1927
accepted.x: The 2023 amendment renamed it the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact official title from plausible but unofficial alternatives.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 was enforced in
o: January 2022
April 2024
October 2022
April 2023
accepted.x: Although enacted in 2022, the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act was enforced in April 2023.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of enactment from the year of enforcement.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 originally contained
o: 66 sections arranged in 4 chapters
62 sections arranged in 6 chapters
66 sections arranged in 7 chapters
72 sections arranged in 7 chapters
accepted.x: The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 contained 66 sections in 7 chapters and was subsequently amended in 1991, 2002, 2006 and 2022.
accepted.tq: Match the numerical structure of the Act without confusing it with the number of schedules.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the definitions in the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 is correct?
o: Wildlife is defined in Section 26 and animal in Section 35.
Section 2(1) defines wildlife, while Section 2(37) defines animal.
Section 2(37) defines wildlife, while Section 2(1) defines animal.
Both wildlife and animal are defined in Section 62.
accepted.x: Section 2(37) defines wildlife and Section 2(1) defines animal.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely placed section numbers and their assigned definitions.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, the term “animal” includes
o: only mammals and birds found in forests
only domesticated animals and their young
plants, fungi and microorganisms occurring in wildlife habitats
amphibians, birds, mammals, reptiles, their young, and the eggs of birds and reptiles
accepted.x: The statutory definition includes amphibians, birds, mammals, reptiles and their young, along with the eggs of birds and reptiles.
accepted.tq: Choose the complete statutory definition rather than a narrower everyday meaning.
accepted.sec: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the schedules of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 after the 2022 amendment, consider the following statements:
1. Schedule I provides the highest protection.
2. Schedule II provides lesser protection.
3. Schedule III contains protected plants.
4. Schedule IV contains specimens listed in the CITES Appendices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements are correct for the four-schedule framework after the 2022 amendment.
accepted.tq: Use the post-amendment schedule structure as a complete classification question.
accepted.sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the schedules before and after the 2022 amendment to the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
o: The number of schedules was increased from four to six.
The separate vermin schedule was retained as Schedule IV.
Protected plants were shifted from Schedule VI to Schedule I without any new schedule structure.
The number of schedules was reduced from six to four.
accepted.x: The 2022 amendment reduced the schedules from six to four and deleted the separate vermin schedule.
accepted.tq: Compare the old and new frameworks by focusing first on the numerical change.
accepted.sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following species-category pairs is correctly matched under the post-2022 schedule framework?
o: Indian flying fox — Schedule II
Indian flying fox — Schedule IV as a CITES specimen
Dugong — Schedule II with lesser protection
Blackbuck — Schedule III as a protected plant
accepted.x: The Indian flying fox was formerly listed as vermin in Schedule V but is placed in Schedule II after the 2022 framework. Blackbuck and dugong are included in Schedule I.
accepted.tq: Track the change in status of a familiar species instead of applying the old vermin classification.
accepted.sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Schedule IV of the Wild Life (Protection) Act after the 2022 amendment:
1. It contains specimens listed in the CITES Appendices.
2. It is the schedule for protected plants.
3. It is the schedule for invasive alien species.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
accepted.x: Schedule IV contains CITES-listed specimens. Protected plants are in Schedule III, while invasive alien species are regulated through a separate power of the Centre.
accepted.tq: Reject options that swap neighbouring schedule subjects and statutory powers.
accepted.sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After deletion of the separate vermin schedule, which authority may declare a wild animal not included in Schedule I as vermin?
o: The National Board for Wildlife through a judicial order
The local authority without any restriction on area or period
The Central Government by notification under Section 62
The State Legislature by amendment of Schedule I
accepted.x: Under Section 62, the Central Government may declare a wild animal not in Schedule I as vermin for a specified area and period by notification.
accepted.tq: Ask who would perform the statutory power and check its area-and-period limits.
accepted.sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of inclusion of an animal in Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
o: The species may be hunted freely without restriction during the notified period.
Hunting and trade are generally prohibited except in special cases allowed by the Act.
Offences attract the heaviest penalties.
The species receives the highest statutory protection.
accepted.x: Schedule I species receive the highest protection; hunting and trade are prohibited except in special cases permitted by the Act. Free hunting is not allowed.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the legal effect of the highest-protection category.
accepted.sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
1. Mugger crocodile — Schedule I
2. Rock eagle-owl — Schedule I
3. Common crow — Schedule I
4. Blackbuck — Schedule I
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The mugger crocodile, rock eagle-owl and blackbuck are in Schedule I. The common crow was included in the former vermin Schedule V, not Schedule I.
accepted.tq: Separate high-protection species from a former vermin species.
accepted.sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A specified plant included in the protected-plant schedule cannot ordinarily be
o: cultivated in every circumstance without regulatory permission
observed or photographed in its natural habitat
picked, uprooted or traded without permission
listed in a scientific publication
accepted.x: A specified plant cannot be picked, uprooted or traded without permission. The law regulates these activities rather than prohibiting observation or scientific description.
accepted.tq: Apply the statutory restriction to the conduct described in the scenario.
accepted.sec: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Indian Forest Act, 1927, which forest category receives the most stringent protection?
o: Village forest
Reserved forest
Protected forest
Community plantation forest
accepted.x: Reserved forests receive the most stringent protection; felling, grazing and hunting are barred unless expressly permitted, and the State controls management.
accepted.tq: Identify the category associated with the strictest restrictions and State control.
accepted.sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A reserved forest is assigned to a village community under which category of the Indian Forest Act, 1927?
o: Cantonment forest
Village forest
Private forest
Protected forest
accepted.x: A village forest is a reserved forest assigned to a village community.
accepted.tq: Use the statutory relationship between a reserved forest and the village-community category.
accepted.sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes a protected forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927?
o: It can be managed only by the Central Government.
All felling, grazing and hunting are automatically barred.
Activities are allowed unless specifically prohibited.
It is a reserved forest assigned to a village community.
accepted.x: In a protected forest, activities are allowed unless specifically prohibited. The relevant provisions are in Chapter IV, Sections 29–34.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the default rule for protected forests from the stricter rule for reserved forests.
accepted.sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which pair correctly indicates the statutory provisions relating to reserved forests and village forests under the Indian Forest Act, 1927?
o: Reserved forests — Sections 3–27; village forests — Section 28
Reserved forests — Sections 29–34; village forests — Section 35
Reserved forests — Section 26 only; village forests — Sections 3–27
Reserved forests — Section 62; village forests — Sections 29–34
accepted.x: Reserved forests are covered in Chapter II, Sections 3–27, while village forests are covered in Chapter III, Section 28.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure section range and reject options that shift categories between chapters.
accepted.sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Section 26 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 primarily deals with
o: regulation of forests that are not government property
assignment of reserved forests to village communities
acts prohibited in a reserved forest, including punishable trespass
removal of bamboo from non-forest land without a permit
accepted.x: Section 26 lists prohibited acts in a reserved forest and makes trespass punishable.
accepted.tq: Match the offence section with its specific prohibited conduct.
accepted.sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Section 35 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 empowers the State to regulate
o: only reserved forests owned by the Union Government
the CITES Appendices
forests that are not government property
wild animals declared vermin under Section 62 of the Wildlife Act
accepted.x: Section 35 permits the State to regulate forests that are not government property.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct authority and subject of the statutory power.
accepted.sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 2017 amendment to the Indian Forest Act, enacted as an Act in 2018, removed which item grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree” under Section 2(7)?
o: Bamboo
Sandalwood
Teak
Eucalyptus
accepted.x: The amendment removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of tree under Section 2(7).
accepted.tq: Identify the exact plant involved in the amendment rather than a commercially important tree chosen as a distractor.
accepted.sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was the practical effect of removing bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree” under the 2017 amendment?
o: Bamboo was brought under Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act.
All bamboo cultivation was prohibited on private land.
Bamboo on private or non-forest land could be felled and transported without a permit.
Bamboo could be felled only in reserved forests without a permit.
accepted.x: Bamboo grown on private or non-forest land could thereafter be felled and transported without a permit.
accepted.tq: Translate a definitional amendment into its practical legal consequence.
accepted.sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which criticism of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 encouraged later reforms towards community rights?
o: It gave unrestricted ownership of forests to forest-dwellers.
It dealt exclusively with marine biodiversity.
It was viewed as harming the livelihoods of forest-dwellers.
It abolished all State control over forest management.
accepted.x: The Act has been criticised for harming forest-dwellers’ livelihoods, contributing to reform efforts focused on community rights.
accepted.tq: Link the criticism to the reform direction without confusing it with the Act’s formal forest categories.
accepted.sec: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment  [APPSC]
